title.narrative: Enterprise development support for SMEs and Cooperatives on their transition to formality with a focus on improving productivity, working conditions and environmental sustainability

description.narrative: Government of South Africa places micro enterprise and SME development at the centre of employment creation and economic growth. This necessitates an enabling business environment with an ecosystem that supports productivity and sustainable enterprises conducive to generating job creation and economic growth. Some of the priority sectors of the economy such as construction, are characterized by gross decent work deficits and poor business practices that do not augur well for productivity and growth. The South African economy operates in a global economy in which there increasing demand for green energy inputs into exports produced by enterprises, and a global business environment that needs such enterprises to adhere to human rights and responsible business practices, and to pay due diligence to wider social and environmental issues, including in supply chains. The strategy will focus on capacity, technical and policy support to assist national efforts at creating an enabling environment and ecosystem to support the promotion of sustainable enterprises, productivity, decent work, and formalization, with a particular focus on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and informal businesses in selected sectors of the economy and to increase their access to supply chain opportunities; capacity support at the national and sub-national level to manage an all-inclusive just transition process and the enabling environment for green business development; and capacity support to enterprises to adopt responsible business practices and circular business models. Sectors targeted for support include construction, the automotive, leather, and footwear, clothing manufacturing and waste management.
